b61.why: 'He crossed the Atlantic': suitcase pose = travelling, walk + pan right carry him across the deck toward the new continent

b61.caption: Prohibition
b61.why: 'found a bigger stage': open-palm presenting pose sweeps at the city while the camera pulls out to reveal how big the stage is

b62.why: 'He built a little wooden box': finger-up eureka pose = the inventor with a clever plan; slow drift lets the idea settle before the box appears
'told buyers it printed perfect hundred dollar bills': Lustig offers the box, bills pop out between them, pan lands on the buyer's amazed face

b63.caption: Tens of thousands
b63.why: 'He sold it for tens of thousands of dollars': palm-up Lustig receives while the buyer hands over a cash stack that slides up between them; push sells the size of the deal

x23.caption: 2 real bills in
x23.why: 'Two real bills went in': teaching finger-up pose, flipped to the right side this time, while two bills drop toward the box on the left; gentle drift for the calm explainer

x23.caption: 6 hours later
x23.why: 'Six hours later, two bills came out': locked-off hold on Lustig with the box, as if sitting out the six hours; flash and the 'copies' pop out on cue

x24.why: 'the extra bills were also real. Hidden in the box': Lustig fans the real bills he hid with a satisfied smirk while more slide up from the hidden compartment; slow drift lets us in on the trick without a shush
'The buyer saw a miracle': amazed buyer alone centre with the 'printed' bills, flash on the reveal
'and paid for a miracle': buyer hands over cash, pan left to Lustig's open palm receiving it while his packed case pops up behind him = the payout is already leaving

x25.why: 'A sheriff in Texas paid thirty thousand dollars for one': Lustig walks in with the box, the badge-wearing sheriff pushes a fat stack across, dusty push
'By the time he understood, Lustig was long gone': sheriff fumes centre as a small suitcase Lustig walks out of frame right, pull widens the empty street

b64.caption: Al Capone
b64.why: 'Then came the boldest move. Al Capone.': Lustig steps forward with his hand out for a handshake, walking straight up to the most dangerous man in Chicago; Capone pops in larger on his name with a flash, push = stakes rising

b65.why: 'He told Capone he needed fifty thousand dollars for an investment': open-palm pitch pose walks up to the seated boss, pan follows the pitch to its target
'promised to double it in sixty days': finger-up promise pose, bills pop beside him; an easy drift = the promise sounds effortless

b66.why: 'Capone gave him the money': Capone pushes the stack across, pan left to Lustig accepting with a hand on his heart and a gracious nod, not grabbing

b66.caption: "Do not make me regret it."
b66.why: 'and a warning. Do not make me regret it.': close, hard push (the strongest in the act) on Capone's wagging finger with a small shake, the money still on the desk as the stakes

b67.caption: Safe deposit box
b67.why: 'Lustig put it in a safe deposit box': locked-off hold on the vault as he walks in carrying the cash case and the deposit-box keys drop in = locked away, nothing moves

b67.caption: 60 days. Nothing.
b67.why: 'and did nothing with it. For two months.': idle hands-behind-back waiting pose, a barely-moving drift = time passing with nothing happening

b68.why: 'Then he walked back': walking-profile Lustig crosses the street, pan right tracks him back toward Capone's door

b68.caption: "The deal fell through."
b68.why: 'with a sad face. The deal fell through, sorry.': hat-in-hands sad pose facing a looming Capone, push into the apology

b69.caption: Every dollar
b69.why: 'He returned every dollar': Lustig holds the whole stack out to Capone, the full pile slides back across the desk
'so impressed by his honesty that he gave him five thousand': Capone now hands money the other way, Lustig's open palm receives, coin pops as the reward

x26.why: 'Think about what Capone saw': Capone alone, hand on chin, slow drift = his thoughts wandering back over the deal
'A man with money in his hands, and he gave it all back': Capone's POV of Lustig holding out the full stack, pull out frames the act as a memory

x27.why: 'In a world of liars, here was the one honest man': calm Lustig centred between shifty gangsters, pull widens the world of liars around him
'the one honest man': ironic tag, Lustig close with a hand on his heart and a sincere nod (the same gracious pose he took the money with); a still hold plays it straight and lets us see the act

b70.why: 'That was the whole point': finger-up key-point pose; a still hold lets the thesis land plainly before the reveal
'The money was never the con': shrug while the cash drops on his right unnoticed; pan left moves away from the money

b70.caption: The trust was.
b70.why: 'The trust was.': Lustig walks out with his case and Capone's trust, Capone appears nodding behind him, coin + flash on the last word; push closes the act on 'can he still win'

needed_plates.desc: First-class promenade deck of a 1920s transatlantic ocean liner by day: white railing at y ~58%, open sea and horizon behind, lifeboats and a funnel at top right, wooden deck chairs at far left; teak deck floor from y ~64% down fully open, centre x 20-80% clear for actors

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash 1930s New York street at night, 16:9: brick tenements and a lit pawnshop/bank front on the right third, fire escapes, wet asphalt reflecting yellow streetlamps, a parked black 1930s sedan far right; open empty pavement foreground y 62-100% across x 15-80% for stick figures standing feet ~y 83%; no people, no text.

Dim 1920s American back room / hotel suite workroom: single green-shaded hanging lamp, wooden workbench at right with tools and a small mahogany box with brass crank, venetian blinds, wallpaper; wooden floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre

Dusty 1920s small Texas town main street, bright day, false-front wooden storefronts, a sheriff's office sign right, water tower and a parked Model-T, tumbleweed; sandy ground y 64-100% open across full width

1920s Chicago street at night, hand-drawn ink and watercolour style matching the Paris plates: brick buildings with fire escapes, neon-less painted speakeasy sign, a parked black 1920s sedan at far right (x 80-100%), lamp posts at x ~12% and ~88%, wet asphalt from y ~63% down fully open, centre x 20-80% clear for two actors

Al Capone's 1920s Chicago hotel office (Lexington Hotel): dark wood panelling, big mahogany desk right of centre (x 60-85%) with ashtray and phone, leather chair, framed portrait, window with blinds and city lights; wooden floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre
1920s American bank vault: wall of brass safe-deposit boxes left-to-right, massive round steel vault door open at right (x 70-95%), marble floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre

Victor Lustig, front-on, flat cap held in both hands at chest, shoulders slumped, sad droopy eyebrows, small frown, eyes looking down (performed sadness)

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret) walking in right-facing profile mid-stride, brown brass-cornered suitcase in the trailing hand, hurried focused look.
Victor Lustig facing right, both arms extended forward holding out a thick stack of green dollar bills, earnest open face, eyebrows raised (handing money over)
American 1920s mark (brown three-piece suit, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, both hands up open, eyes huge and starry, jaw dropped in wonder
Same American mark (brown suit, bowler hat, moustache) facing right, one arm extended handing a fat wad of dollar bills, eager grin
1920s Texas sheriff (tan cowboy hat, star badge, vest, holster, boots, droopy moustache) facing right, holding out a thick wad of dollar bills, greedy grin
Same Texas sheriff front-on, fists clenched, red face, steam puffs from ears, furious frown, hat askew

Al Capone stick figure in the same hand-drawn ink style (white round head, long black stick limbs): grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar in mouth, arms crossed, heavy scowl with one eyebrow down; standing front-on, slight right turn; full body on flat magenta background

Al Capone (same as capone_1: white round head, long black stick limbs, grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar) seated behind a mahogany desk facing right, fingers steepled, cigar smoke curling, appraising squint

Al Capone (same as capone_1: white round head, long black stick limbs, grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar) standing facing right, one arm extended holding out a stack of dollar bills, small approving smile

Al Capone (same as capone_1: white round head, long black stick limbs, grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar) front-on close stance, leaning forward, index finger raised and wagging, cigar clenched, narrowed threatening eyes

Al Capone (same as capone_1: white round head, long black stick limbs, grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar) front-on, one hand stroking chin, other hand holding cigar, eyebrows raised, impressed and thoughtful
1920s Chicago gangster henchman (black fedora, dark pinstripe suit, loud tie), front-on, hands in pockets, eyes sliding sideways, sly crooked grin (a liar)
